title: Thesis: local interaction telemetry for the user study
description: Privacy-focused local interaction logging for the thesis user study (and dogfood metrics): branch created, checkpoint restored/switched, compare/diff viewed, apply accepted, time-on-node; written locally under .evograph/ (e.g. telemetry.jsonl), no network, study-mode opt-in. Must land before the study runs (target: alongside M3/M4). Feeds the protocol's telemetry metric and M_HT analysis.

title: M0: scaffold checkpoint core (shadow-git store, checkpoint types, restore)
description: M0 scaffold of the non-linear interface core (fusion product; decisions ratified 2026-10-24). Deliverable: VS Code extension scaffold in extension/ with the shadow-git checkpoint store at <workspace>/.evograph/, checkpoint types (origin/manual/ai_prompt/ai_applied) modeled in the schema, manual + origin capture with auto-generated titles/descriptions (heuristic summarizer; LLM provider pluggable later), restore-to-checkpoint, persistence across reloads. Docs: history/nonlinear-interface-mini-spec.md and section 8 of history/evograph-ide-execution-brief.md. Fusion scope: one development graph as the system of record; IDE authoring surface first (M0-M4), read-only manager web view last (M5). v1 users: solo developers with AI assistants. Passivity: passive-first with optional one-keystroke confirmations.
design: Mini-spec: history/nonlinear-interface-mini-spec.md. Brief: history/evograph-ide-execution-brief.md (section 8). Storage: shadow git repo; checkpoint metadata embedded in commit messages; per-checkpoint refs refs/evograph/checkpoints/<uuid>; active pointer refs/evograph/active.
acceptance_criteria: A 15-minute coding session produces a correct branching history with zero manual git usage; npm run check green (lint, typecheck, tests, compile).
notes: Scaffold complete (2026-10-24): extension/ with shadow-git checkpoint store, engine, commands, 23 tests; npm run check green (lint, typecheck, tests, compile). Remaining: dogfood the 15-minute branching scenario in the Extension Development Host (open extension/ in VS Code, press F5); file friction findings as new issues.
close_reason: M0 dogfood passed (2026-10-24): checkpoint create/restore/branch scenario verified end-to-end in the Extension Development Host on this repo; unit gate green (npm run check, 23 tests). User still learning the flow; friction items to be filed as found.

title: Research EvoGraph IDE: papers, related work, resources
description: Full web research on EvoGraph IDE — research papers, published related work, helpful resources. Determine feasibility of building a Project Management System (PMS) on/around it.
close_reason: Completed: full research dossier at history/evograph-ide-research.md (core papers, related work, resources, PMS feasibility). Session journal updated.

title: Add LICENSE file (concept note describes the apparatus as open-source)
description: The thesis concept note (history/thesis-concept-note.md) describes this repo as an open-source prototype; the repo has no LICENSE file. Pick a license (MIT is consistent with the old PMS draft's stated intent) and add it, then reference it in the README.

title: Study material: benchmark task, seeded trap, NASA-TLX + E_gap instruments
description: Author the thesis study's separate material per history/thesis-experimental-protocol.md: the standardized 45-minute benchmark task repo (stateful data-table component), the seeded hallucination trap plus detection scoring (M_HT), the NASA-TLX instrument, and the 5-question E_gap comprehension quiz. Keep out of product code (study/ folder or separate repo). Timeline tied to the study date.
notes: E_gap template archived (history/thesis-experimental-protocol.md Section 6, 5 questions with scoring); M_CSR metric added (quiz Q5). Concept-note Section 4.3 archived at history/thesis-concept-note.md.

title: M4: graph-as-context + LLM merge v1
description: Graph-as-context: toggle to include the branching checkpoint history (and task intent when linked) in the next prompt, with token-cost awareness. Merge with active: creates a new checkpoint; code merged by the LLM from diffs of both checkpoints against their most recent common ancestor; chat histories merged via a summary message; title and description combined.

title: Fold PMS draft docs into history/pms-draft (extract, no verbatim copy)
description: Extract product-relevant content from ~/my_space/coding/pms_project_management_system_01 (pms_plan.txt, PROJECT_PLAN.md, README.md) into a clean history/pms-draft/ document set for this repo. Do not copy pms_plan.txt verbatim (it contains a personal conversation); keep the old repo as a private archive. Capture: passive-tracking philosophy, Flow State UX ideas, initial schema sketch, and the items this repo demoted to non-goals (microservices, IntelliJ plugin, budget service, OS deep-work timer per brief section 8).

title: M5: manager web view - read-only board as graph projection (first PMS surface)
description: First PMS surface: read-only web app where the board and tasks are projections of the checkpoint graph (no separate PMS database). Per-task exploration trees (which alternatives were tried, which was chosen), human/AI provenance and attribution stats, and an evidence-derived status engine (status changes follow graph evidence; cards are never moved by hand). Web stack decided at that point. This is where the fusion of the non-linear interface and the PMS becomes visible.

title: M2: assistant loop - minimal chat panel + AI checkpoint capture
description: Own minimal chat webview (assistant surface decision): send a prompt, receive a response; ai_prompt checkpoint auto-created on each exchange (editing an earlier prompt creates a branch from that checkpoint); code blocks detected in responses; Apply Changes creates an ai_applied checkpoint; the AI interaction state is restored together with the code state. Pluggable model provider interface (provider choice still open; single provider first). Chat history persisted in the workspace store.
notes: Thesis scope addition (2026-10-24): ai_prompt checkpoints must record provider + model + version so the study run is reproducible (extend checkpoint metadata; likely schemaVersion 2); the model should be pinnable for study runs. See history/thesis-experimental-protocol.md.

title: M1: development history graph panel (webview DAG)
description: Interactive checkpoint DAG in a VS Code webview: nodes color-coded by type (origin/manual/ai_prompt/ai_applied), active-node emphasis, click to switch versions, context menu (activate; delete with child reattachment), branching visible as a DAG. Vocabulary and interaction rules follow the paper and mini-spec section 5 (same terms: checkpoint, branch, active checkpoint). Webview UI stack decided at M1 start; impeccable init provides the design system. Depends on M0.

title: M3: compare + Review Mode + passive task linking
description: Compare with active: temporary diff tab showing differences in code and AI interaction states between two checkpoints. Review Mode: inline provenance annotations since origin (green = human, blue = AI) with hover responsible-node tooltip (file, description, type, timestamp, id) that highlights the node. Passive-first task linking per mini-spec section 6: after a branch of unattributed checkpoints, offer one-keystroke link suggestions; dismissible; a visible unattributed backlog; never a required form.

title: Choose a distinct product name (avoid EvoGraph collisions)
description: Dossier section 1 lists 14+ distinct works named EvoGraph. Do not ship any public artifact (marketplace listing, public repo rename, site) under that name. Shortlist distinct names, check availability on npm/vsce/marketplace and general web, then decide. Not urgent for local development.
